scope: Independent scientific and numerical review of the paid tethering benchmark. Checked the fixed-family certificate and its public interpretation. Review covers the declared finite-grid claim.
scientific_conclusion: The checked finite-lattice result supports a small positive gap to the best constant paid-channel prefactor at T=2 on the n=48 grid. It establishes neither a continuum advantage nor superiority to all constant or passive physical architectures.
checked_invariants: Paid and passive tether transitions retain their paired reverse and matching position-dependent equilibrium flux, including zero propensity for both directions of the last spectator edge.
Both designs have the same Gibbs reference, initial law and fuel/waste energy scale. The spectator assumption changes permitted kinetics. Actual fabrication and recognition costs have no calibration.
Spatial neighbor fluxes satisfy the common Gibbs law. Lumping the even periodic cubic lattice by whole-coordinate reflections and permutations preserves rates and launch multiplicities.
The killed generator retains the thermal damage exit rate in HD. The stopped fuel and tether moments account for values at absorption.

The certified constant generator is affine in alpha. Conditional Poisson interleaving, first and second differences, bounded discarded weights and Taylor box splitting furnish a global enclosure. The interval logic preserved positivity, discarded-tail scope and derivative signs in the tested cases.

findings.finding: A fourth strongly applied continuum generator requires a domain argument because Metropolis acceptance has a kink.
findings.resolution: Verified source now explicitly scopes the Taylor identities to the finite lattices.

findings.finding: An upper endpoint for the gap to the best fixed design does not bound the gap to every weaker fixed design.
findings.resolution: Verified source now refers to the optimum over the fixed interval.

findings.finding: Alpha=1 is the sampled fixed comparator at the finest certified grid. The global certificate encloses the best fixed value without identifying its exact optimizer.
findings.resolution: Report alpha=1 as the common plotted fixed sample and the main gap relative to the certified optimum.

findings.finding: The Euler-SDE check has insufficient precision to discriminate the policy gap. The no-well ablation changes conformation energetics along with force.
findings.resolution: Both scope limits appear in the reviewed manuscript.
